questions.stem: On what is Data Categorisation based?
options: The business requirements of the organisation
The attributes and properties of the entities in a dataset
The order in which data was loaded
The cost of storing the data
questions.explanation: Categorisation is based on the attributes and properties of entities in the dataset, whereas classification is based on business requirements.

questions.stem: On what is Data Classification based, as distinct from Data Categorisation?
options: The file format of the data
The physical location of the server
questions.explanation: Classification is driven by business requirements, such as grouping categories into risk levels or family versus non-family members.

questions.stem: What do Data Categorisation and Data Classification both count as, and what are they used for?
options: Both are Metadata and are used for Data Governance
Both are encryption methods used for Data Security
Both are storage formats used for archiving
Both are database indexes used for performance
Both are reporting tools used for dashboards
questions.explanation: Both Categorisation and Classification are Metadata and are used for Data Governance as well.

questions.stem: In the Data Science domain, under which learning method do Data Categorisation and Data Classification fall?
options: Neither; they are not part of Machine Learning
questions.explanation: Both terms fall under Supervised Learning in the Data Science domain.

questions.stem: In the household example from I Am Datapedia!, which of the following is a classification rather than a category?
questions.explanation: Grandparents, parents, children, cousins, gardener, mechanic and car painters are categories; family members and non-family members are the classifications built on them.

questions.stem: In the household example from I Am Datapedia!, which of the following is a category?
questions.explanation: Gardener is one of the categories; family members and non-family members are the classifications.

questions.stem: In the I Am Datapedia! example of documents, categories such as passport, health record, financial record and job posting were all classified as what?
questions.explanation: The data was categorised into passport, health record, financial record and job posting, and those categories were classified as Medium Risk.

questions.stem: Why is the distinction between Data Categorisation and Data Classification described as confusing?
options: Because neither term is defined anywhere
Because both are types of encryption
Because the two terms are often used interchangeably
Because only data scientists are allowed to use them
Because they apply only to unstructured data
questions.explanation: Categorisation and Classification are used interchangeably in practice, even though categorisation reflects entity attributes and classification reflects business requirements.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as a category in the household example from I Am Datapedia!?
questions.explanation: The listed categories are grandparents, parents, children, cousins, servants, gardener, mechanic and car painters; neighbours are not among them.

questions.stem: In the household example from I Am Datapedia!, under which classification would a car painter fall?
questions.explanation: Gardener, mechanic, car painters and servants are classified as non-family members.
